changelog: feat: a results view in the beta console, plus the settings dropdowns and step colours. (1) GET /results/{job_id}/log is new, and fixes a finished run showing an EMPTY log. /progress serves the log from the in-memory job dict — capped at 500 lines and gone after a restart — so the first real run through the beta finished with '(no log lines yet) · 0 lines', which reads as 'this produced no output' on exactly the job someone is looking back at. pipeline.log was on disk the whole time. The beta now falls back to it, says when the log came off disk and that it is the tail of a longer file, and when BOTH copies are gone says so and adds that this implies nothing about whether the run worked. (2) The step settings are dropdowns again, with the production console's own option lists and wording: nbases 10M/100M/500M, pool, chimera method, codon table, ONT and PacBio regions, Top 30/50/100, the ambiguous-read choice. A select whose values are all numeric now posts numbers — nbases had become a dropdown that would otherwise have started sending the string '100000000', which pydantic coerces, so nothing would have failed loudly. (3) Each step card carries a hue keyed to its step NUMBER, so Step 5 is the same colour on a 16S job as on an ONT job where the steps before it differ; step 1b shares step 1's hue because it is part of step 1. The eight hues are the validated categorical palette (adjacent-pair CVD dE 9.1 light / 8.4 dark, run through the validator; a substitute to avoid red failed the chroma floor, so the documented set is used unchanged). Colour is never the only signal — the number badge and the title carry identity. Dark mode has its own steps, not a flip. (4) The results view lists the job's CSV tables and PDF figures, previews a table immediately with its row and column counts and numeric columns right-aligned, opens figures inline, and links to the zip and to chart customisation. taxonomy_genus.csv is sorted to the top because alphabetical order buries it. Chart customisation still opens the production console on purpose: it writes into the job's settings file, and two editors on one settings file is how a saved palette loses half its colours.
